spans.s: śabda, same as mahā-śabda; cf. pañca-śabda (BL).
Sabrahmacārin (CII 3), a religious student of a group that follows the same śākhā.

sa-bāhy-ābhyantar-ādāya , ‘together with the external and internal income or taxes to be paid to the state and to the village authorities’; epithet of the gift village; cf. abhyantara-siddhyā, etc. Cf. Ind. Ep., p. 395.
